# Lab 10.9: BigQuery Omni: AWS & Azure

## What We Are Going to Do
Query Parquet files in Amazon S3 with BigQuery Omni, without moving them, then copy a result into a Google Cloud dataset. You need an AWS account.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create an AWS connection.** **+ Add data → Connections to external data sources → AWS (via BigLake)**:
   - **Connection ID**: `lab_aws`
   - **Location**: `aws-us-east-1`
   - **AWS role ID**: `arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/bq-omni-role`

   Copy the **BigQuery Google identity** shown after creation.

2. **In AWS, create the role.** Create `bq-omni-role` with S3 read access to your bucket, and a trust policy for `accounts.google.com` with the Google identity from step 1 as `accounts.google.com:sub`.

3. **[CLI] Create a dataset in the AWS region.**

4. **[SQL] Create and query the table.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT` and the S3 path.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE lab10_aws.sales_s3
WITH CONNECTION `YOUR_PROJECT.aws-us-east-1.lab_aws`
OPTIONS (format = 'PARQUET', uris = ['s3://my-bq-lab-bucket/sales/*']);

SELECT city, SUM(amount) AS total FROM lab10_aws.sales_s3 GROUP BY city;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The query runs in AWS. Only the small result comes back.

5. **[SQL] Copy a result into Google Cloud.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab10.sales_from_aws AS
SELECT city, SUM(amount) AS total FROM lab10_aws.sales_s3 GROUP BY city;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   This cross-cloud CTAS moves only the result, and you pay AWS egress for it.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Compute | Runs in the AWS region |
| Data | Stays in S3 |
| Auth | AWS IAM role trusted by Google identity |
| Cross-cloud copy | CTAS into a US dataset |
